commit_message:
[json] Use map cache for stringify fast-path

We expect that many objects will share the same map, so we can cache
some interesting properties per map that we have fully serialized.
Namely:
- Are all properties enumerable.
- No property key is a symbol.
- No property key contains characters that require escaping.

When serializing an object with a map known to fulfill these
properties, we can omit a bunch of checks.

findings.title: Incorrect field index assumption in ResumeJSObject for kBuildingMapCache mode
findings.message: When building the map cache (mode == kBuildingMapCache), the ResumeJSObject function incorrectly uses `descriptor_idx` directly as `property_index` instead of `details.field_index()`. The optimization of using the descriptor number as the field index is only valid for the fast-map-cache case (kWithMapCache), where all properties are guaranteed to be consecutive, enumerable, and stored as in-object fields in descriptor order. For kBuildingMapCache mode, the map is not yet validated as fast, so property field indices can differ from their descriptor indices. This causes a DCHECK failure in debug builds and incorrect property slot access in release builds, potentially reading the wrong property value or accessing memory out of the intended object layout.
findings.suggestion: Move the `int property_index` declaration inside the conditional branches so that the non-fast (kBuildingMapCache / kWithoutMapCache) branch assigns `property_index = details.field_index()` and only the kWithMapCache branch assigns `property_index = descriptor_idx`. This matches the fix applied in ba4aa40.

ground_truth.root_cause: In the introducing commit (7ad549886aa), the code was refactored to use `descriptor_idx` directly as `property_index` (an optimization assuming descriptor order equals field order) but the assignment `int property_index = descriptor_idx;` was placed unconditionally outside the `if constexpr (mode != ResumeJSObjectMode::kWithMapCache)` block. This means the `kBuildingMapCache` branch also uses `descriptor_idx` as the field index, despite not having yet validated that the map's fields are in descriptor order.
